policy: kill first; SPAN_UNDERIVED candidates are ineligible (R377 evidence-derivation requirement); R397 Phase 2: DOES_NOT_BEAT_BASELINE and PLAUSIBILITY_BOUND_VIOLATED candidates are ineligible for release (the machine's own physics gates the claim); among survivors prefer better E15-B verdict, then BEATS_BASELINE, then fewer deficient areas, then fewer UNCERTAIN attack outcomes; NO numeric score is computed (CEO standing rule: no new scoring systems)

ranked.mechanism: Decoupling fuselage pitch attitude from wing angle of attack via variable-incidence aerodynamic surfaces to maintain optimal lift-to-drag performance across varying speeds.
ranked.intervention: Design a high-performance ground vehicle with active, variable-incidence aerodynamic surfaces (e.g., flaps, canards, or splitter adjustments) driven by lightweight actuators to independently optimize local AoA while keeping the vehicle body stable, thereby minimizing parasitic drag and rotor/airflow interference at extreme velocities.

ranked.mechanism: Decoupling pitch attitude from wing angle of attack to maintain optimal lift-to-drag performance
ranked.intervention: Integrate a variable-incidence front spoiler or fixed-wing aerodynamic surface with a dual-actuator drive system that adjusts angle of attack independently of vehicle body pitch

ranked.mechanism: Decoupling aerodynamic surfaces from the main vehicle body via variable incidence to optimize lift-to-drag ratio across varying speeds while maintaining stability.
ranked.intervention: Implement variable-incidence rear aerodynamic elements (spoilers or wings) on the high-performance ground vehicle with dual-actuator drive systems to independently adjust angle of attack separate from vehicle pitch/attitude during high-speed travel.

ranked.mechanism: Decoupling fuselage attitude from wing aerodynamics using a variable-incidence lifting surface and dual-actuator drive system.
ranked.intervention: Implement an active, variable-incidence rear wing on the ground vehicle that independently adjusts its angle of attack relative to the chassis pitch to maintain optimal lift-to-drag ratios at extreme velocities.

ranked.mechanism: Decoupling the vehicle's static body attitude from the aerodynamic angle of attack of a passive lifting element allows the element to maintain an optimal lift-to-drag ratio independent of the vehicle's primary pitch orientation, thereby maximizing passive lift and minimizing net aerodynamic drag across varying speeds.
ranked.intervention: Integrate a variable-incidence wing or lifting surface with a dual-actuator drive system that adjusts the angle of attack independently of the chassis pitch, with a total structural mass penalty of 209 g.

ranked.mechanism: Alleviating detrimental rotor-wing interference through variable incidence allows the reestablishment of strong suction peaks on the upper surface of the lifting element, which maximizes passive lift generation and reduces the power required from the primary thrust systems to maintain speed.
ranked.intervention: Configure the control strategy to specifically target the alleviation of interference effects by adjusting the wing AoA to 10°-12° when the fuselage pitch is -20°, utilizing high-fidelity CFD-optimized profiles.

ranked.mechanism: Decoupling fuselage attitude from wing aerodynamics enables the vehicle to maintain optimal lift-to-drag performance across varying flight speeds, providing a robust and highly efficient solution for extending endurance in energy-constrained environments by allowing the vehicle to adapt its aerodynamic profile independently of its stability attitude.
ranked.intervention: Implement a decoupling control strategy that allows the lifting wing to adjust its incidence to optimize efficiency without constraining the main vehicle's pitch attitude, utilizing a lightweight 143 g wing structure.

ranked.mechanism: Real-time optimization of body attitude and active ground-effect skirt gap via variable-incidence aerodynamic surfaces to minimize parasitic drag, mitigate high-speed lift-induced instability, and reduce energy losses from boundary layer separation.
ranked.intervention: Implement a closed-loop control system using lightweight actuators to dynamically adjust the angle of fixed body panels (e.g., front splitters, rear diffusers) and maintain an optimal ground clearance. This actively manages the pressure distribution under the chassis and around the wheels to counteract lift and streamline airflow, independent of wheel rotation or lift generation.

selection_basis.intervention: Design a high-performance ground vehicle with active, variable-incidence aerodynamic surfaces (e.g., flaps, canards, or splitter adjustments) driven by lightweight actuators to independently optimize local AoA while keeping the vehicle body stable, thereby minimizing parasitic drag and rotor/airflow interference at extreme velocities.
